journal_name: Annals of Pure and Applied Logic

abstracts.abstract: The relationship between intensional and extensional semantics in logical systems has long been recognized as a fundamental concern in mathematical logic. Traditional approaches have typically treated these as separate domains with limited interaction. This paper develops a novel categorical framework that unifies intensional and extensional interpretations through a generalized presheaf construction. Our approach leverages the profound interplay between syntax and semantics by introducing a new notion of mixed morphisms that simultaneously capture both intensional context and extensional content. The framework is characterized by a universal property that subsumes existing correspondence theories as special cases. We demonstrate that this unification yields new insights into the structure of logical systems, including a characterization theorem establishing that semantic properties can be constructively captured through syntactic invariants. The categorical semantics reveals unexpected connections between previously disparate areas of pure logic, opening directions for research in algebraic logic and categorical logic. This work represents a paradigm shift in how we understand the relationship between different logical semantics, providing a unified perspective that has not been previously available in the literature.

The development of strong consistency results for logical systems remains one of the central challenges in proof theory. This paper establishes a significant strengthening of the Gödel-Malcev theorem for a broad class of non-classical logics by introducing a refined analysis of consistency proofs based on novel applications of the subformula property. We develop a technique that combines structural proof theory with algebraic methods in a way that yields substantially sharper results than previous approaches. The method proceeds by constructing a canonical extension of any consistent theory to a prime filter, exploiting the interaction between syntactic and algebraic properties of the underlying logic. As consequences of our main theorem, we obtain improved bounds on the size of consistency proofs and establish new conservativity results between different logical systems. The analysis applies uniformly to intuitionistic logic augmented with various combination principles, providing a unified treatment that subsumes several previously separate investigations. These results have significant implications for the proof-theoretic program of understanding the constructive content of logical reasoning, advancing our understanding of the structural properties of proof systems.

Modern proof assistants demand logical foundations that simultaneously support expressive specification and reliable computation. We introduce the Indexed Linear Type Theory (ILTT), a new type-theoretic framework that fundamentally reconciles linear reasoning with dependent types. Unlike existing approaches that either restrict linearity to base types or abandon computational properties, ILTT provides a uniform treatment of resources across all type levels through a novel indexing mechanism. The system design incorporates a bidirectional typing discipline that ensures principal typing while maintaining decidable type checking. We develop a complete categorical semantics for ILTT in the setting of indexed categories with computational traces, establishing that the framework satisfies the expected conservativity properties over existing systems. The practical significance of ILTT is demonstrated through extended examples in verification of stateful programs, protocol specifications, and quantum computing paradigms. The normalization theorem for the system ensures that all well-typed programs terminate, providing the guarantees required for trustworthy formal verification. This work offers a new paradigm for logical foundations of computation that has not been previously achievable.

The formalization of mathematical reasoning in computational proof assistants requires logical systems that support increasingly complex structures while preserving essential properties such as normalization. We present a significant enhancement of the Calculus of Inductive Constructions that addresses critical limitations in handling higher-order quantification over dependent families. Our extended system introduces a refined universe hierarchy with cumulative definitional equality, substantially improving the expressive power available for formalization while maintaining syntactic safety. The technical core of our contribution lies in a new reduction strategy that eliminates critical pairs arising from universe polymorphism, enabling a more elegant treatment of large-scale mathematical formalization. We establish metatheoretic properties including strong normalization through a novel technique combining reducibility with forcing at the level of the syntactic theory itself. The practical impact is evaluated through case studies in formalizing substantial results from algebraic geometry and category theory, where previous systems encountered fundamental barriers. The work provides both a practical tool for working mathematicians and a theoretical contribution to our understanding of type-theoretic foundations.
